- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for early periods.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >80), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment shows positive bias (e.g., >0.20), model underestimates upside; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — if 30d forecast is flat or rising slowly, true outcome often diverges sharply; add volatility buffer (±2–5%) to forecast range.
- If sentiment history shows increasing negativity (e.g., 0.33, 0.00, 0.00), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias.
- For 30d horizon, avoid linear extrapolation — true outcomes often show non-linear corrections; use exponential decay or moving average smoothing for trend correction.
